title: Student HMO landlords sell 2,000 beds amid regulatory shift
summary:
Landlords have disposed of at least 2,000 student HMO beds across Britain over the past year, responding to the Renters' Rights Act and increased regulatory requirements. Specialist estate agency YieldMe reports handling £170 million worth of HMO sales in the 12-month period.

title: Strutt & Parker creates role for prime city markets
summary:
Strutt & Parker has created a new senior position focused on prime residential markets in England's cathedral and university cities, appointing Louise Glanville as its first Head of National Town and City Markets. Glanville joins as a Director after nearly ten years at Knight Frank, where she served as Partner and Head of the Exeter office.

title: Manchester overtakes London as top buy-to-let location
summary:
Manchester has surpassed London as the most sought-after location for buy-to-let investors, with 23% targeting the city compared to 18% focusing on the capital. The shift reflects investor preference for Manchester's 6.6% gross rental yields against London's 5.1%.

title: Proptech firm launches service to speed property sales
summary:
Proptech company iamproperty has introduced a new service designed to accelerate property transactions by preparing documentation earlier in the sales process. The service, called Sale Ready, can reduce transaction times by an average of four weeks according to the company.

title: Estate agents shift focus to buyers as market rebalances
summary:
Estate agents may need to reorient their business models towards buyers rather than sellers as market conditions shift, according to industry commentary analysing recent property market data. Recent figures from Zoopla indicate buyer demand has fallen 10% year-on-year in May, while Rightmove reports that buyer choice has reached its highest level since 2015.

title: Government proposes First Time Buyer ISA to replace Lifetime ISA
summary:
The government has published consultation proposals to replace the Lifetime ISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA, removing the retirement savings component and withdrawal penalties. Financial services firms have welcomed the simplification whilst warning that high property prices and deposit requirements remain the primary barriers to homeownership.

title: £2.95m bridging loan funds Liverpool apartment development
summary:
District & County Investments has provided a £2.95m net bridging facility to support a brownfield regeneration project in Liverpool city centre, which will deliver more than 150 apartments upon completion. The transaction highlights growing demand for planning bridge finance as Building Safety Regulation requirements add complexity to development timelines.

title: Knight Frank enters redundancy consultation process
summary:
Knight Frank has initiated a redundancy consultation affecting less than 3% of its UK workforce, despite posting a 6.3% increase in annual revenues. The agency confirmed the consultation is underway but declined to specify which departments or how many roles are under review.

title: Kent letting agent fined £15,000 for client money breach
summary:
A Kent-based letting agency has paid a £15,000 civil penalty after operating without required client money protection. Homelet PMS Ltd was fined by Medway Council for breaching regulations that mandate all letting agents handling client funds must belong to an approved protection scheme.
